eli: Heads-up: I'm seeing a handful of community issues where the Quickstart fails on fresh installs because of faraday/oauth2 conflicts. Thinking we should do a short-term "minimal" gem and a longer-term split. Thoughts?

harper: Can you paste an example error?

eli: Sure, from a user report: ```Bundler could not find compatible versions for gem "faraday": In snapshot: faraday (= 2.0.0) In Gemfile: some-plugin (~> 1.2) depends on faraday (~> 1.8)``` They installed the full sdk for a tiny generation example.

sophia: Agree this is hurting onboarding. We discussed splitting before; maybe publish a `redwood-minimal` that includes the core HTTP/stream primitives but no oauth or heavy deps. Keep `redwood` as the full, backwards-compatible gem.

jorge: Parity flag: streaming retry and auth refresh are currently intertwined. If minimal lacks auth, we must ensure core exposes a refresh hook so `redwood-auth` can re-register the same behavior. Otherwise users will hit subtle reconnect/retry regressions.

eli: Proposed lightweight hook API (very small):```ruby
# register in auth gem
Redwood::Core.before_stream_retry do |ctx|
  Auth::Refresher.maybe_refresh(ctx)
end
```

harper: That looks fine. For compatibility, we can keep a shim in `redwood` that requires both gems. Migration notes in CHANGELOG.

sophia: CI suggestion: add a matrix job installing only the minimal gem and running Quickstart smoke. Right now our smoke installs the monolith only, so we never catch minimal-install edge cases.

ci-bot: build #1203 ruby-3.2 matrix failed: bundler conflict. Log excerpt: "Bundler could not find compatible versions for gem \"faraday\": In snapshot: faraday (= 2.0.0) In Gemfile: some-plugin (~> 1.2) depends on faraday (~> 1.8)"

eli: That's the motivator. Action items I propose: 1) draft RFC for split + deprecation timeline; 2) implement `redwood-core` with hook API; 3) publish `redwood-minimal` alpha; 4) add core-only CI job and Quickstart variant; 5) small test to ensure stream parity with and without auth hook.

harper: +1. I'll review the RFC and help with CI. Can you also include a tiny sample showing manual auth hookup for environments that roll their own tokens?

jorge: I'll prototype the hook and add unit tests that assert identical reconnect sequence when hook is a noop vs when auth refresher is attached.

sophia: I'll update Quickstart to call out `gem install redwood-minimal` for constrained envs and add troubleshooting note for bundler conflicts.

eli: Thanks all. Draft RFC here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-sdk/pull/521 (WIP). Tagging reviewers.
